title: Frogs and mosquitoes
statementMd:
There are $*n*$ frogs sitting on the coordinate axis $*Ox*$. For each frog two values $*x*_{*i*}, *t*_{*i*}$ are known — the position and the initial length of the tongue of the $*i*$-th frog (it is guaranteed that all positions $*x*_{*i*}$ are different). $*m*$ mosquitoes one by one are landing to the coordinate axis. For each mosquito two values are known $*p*_{*j*}$ — the coordinate of the position where the $*j*$-th mosquito lands and $*b*_{*j*}$ — the size of the $*j*$-th mosquito. Frogs and mosquitoes are represented as points on the coordinate axis.

The frog can eat mosquito if mosquito is in the same position with the frog or to the right, and the distance between them is not greater than the length of the tongue of the frog.

If at some moment several frogs can eat a mosquito the leftmost frog will eat it (with minimal $*x*_{*i*}$). After eating a mosquito the length of the tongue of a frog increases with the value of the size of eaten mosquito. It's possible that after it the frog will be able to eat some other mosquitoes (the frog should eat them in this case).

For each frog print two values — the number of eaten mosquitoes and the length of the tongue after landing all mosquitoes and after eating all possible mosquitoes by frogs.

Each mosquito is landing to the coordinate axis only after frogs eat all possible mosquitoes landed before. Mosquitoes are given in order of their landing to the coordinate axis.

## Input

First line contains two integers $*n*, *m*$ ($1 ≤ *n*, *m* ≤ 2·10^{5}$) — the number of frogs and mosquitoes.

Each of the next $*n*$ lines contains two integers $*x*_{*i*}, *t*_{*i*}$ ($0 ≤ *x*_{*i*}, *t*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{9}$) — the position and the initial length of the tongue of the $*i*$-th frog. It is guaranteed that all $*x*_{*i*}$ are different.

Next $*m*$ lines contain two integers each $*p*_{*j*}, *b*_{*j*}$ ($0 ≤ *p*_{*j*}, *b*_{*j*} ≤ 10^{9}$) — the position and the size of the $*j*$-th mosquito.

## Output

Print $*n*$ lines. The $*i*$-th line should contain two integer values $*c*_{*i*}, *l*_{*i*}$ — the number of mosquitoes eaten by the $*i*$-th frog and the length of the tongue of the $*i*$-th frog.
statementZhMd:
坐标轴 $Ox$ 上坐着 $*n*$ 只青蛙。对于每只青蛙，已知两个值 $*x*_{*i*}, *t*_{*i*}$，分别表示第 $*i*$ 只青蛙的位置和舌头的初始长度（保证所有位置 $*x*_{*i*}$ 互不相同）。有 $*m*$ 只蚊子依次落到坐标轴上。对于每只蚊子，已知两个值 $*p*_{*j*}$ 和 $*b*_{*j*}$，分别表示第 $*j*$ 只蚊子落下的位置坐标和大小。青蛙和蚊子都表示为坐标轴上的点。

当蚊子与青蛙位于同一位置，或位于青蛙的右侧，且二者之间的距离不超过青蛙舌头的长度时，这只青蛙就可以吃掉该蚊子。

如果在某一时刻有多只青蛙可以吃掉一只蚊子，则由最左边的青蛙（即 $*x*_{*i*}$ 最小的青蛙）吃掉它。青蛙吃掉一只蚊子后，其舌头长度会增加所吃蚊子的大小。因此，青蛙可能会因此能够吃掉其他蚊子（在这种情况下，青蛙应当将它们吃掉）。

请对于每只青蛙输出两个值：在所有蚊子落下并且青蛙吃掉所有可能吃掉的蚊子后，该青蛙吃掉的蚊子数量以及舌头的长度。

每只蚊子只有在青蛙吃掉此前已经落下的所有可能吃掉的蚊子后，才会落到坐标轴上。蚊子按照落到坐标轴上的顺序给出。

## 输入格式

第一行包含两个整数 $*n*, *m*$（$1 ≤ *n*, *m* ≤ 2·10^{5}$）——青蛙和蚊子的数量。

接下来的 $*n*$ 行中，每行包含两个整数 $*x*_{*i*}, *t*_{*i*}$（$0 ≤ *x*_{*i*}, *t*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{9}$）——第 $*i*$ 只青蛙的位置和舌头的初始长度。保证所有 $*x*_{*i*}$ 互不相同。

接下来的 $*m*$ 行中，每行包含两个整数 $*p*_{*j*}, *b*_{*j*}$（$0 ≤ *p*_{*j*}, *b*_{*j*} ≤ 10^{9}$）——第 $*j*$ 只蚊子的位置和大小。

## 输出格式

输出 $*n*$ 行。第 $*i*$ 行应包含两个整数 $*c*_{*i*}, *l*_{*i*}$——第 $*i*$ 只青蛙吃掉的蚊子数量以及该青蛙的舌头长度。
